_doc: WS-C (D-6) externalized classification vocabulary for the draft (prose election / scoring / lint) path. era_section_role_tokens is WoW expansion-name vocabulary matched against history section-role identifiers (e.g. 'cataclysm_edit'); it is externalized both to de-duplicate it across prose_election + faction_scoring (principle 5) and so a new expansion is a data update, not a code change. historical_framing_markers is matched against generated/source PROSE text (no section role available at that point), so no structural signal exists. Each entry carries a pilot-bias note (D-6 clause 4).

era_section_role_tokens._why_no_structural_signal: Identifies expansion-named history sections; the expansion name itself is open vocabulary (grows each expansion) with no finer structural signal than the section-role string it appears in.
era_section_role_tokens._pilot_bias_note: All current WoW expansion shorthands; cross-zone (not WPL-specific). Add the next expansion's token here on release.

expansion_release_order._doc: Canonical WoW expansion release order (chronological). Used as a SOFT, RELATIVE recency signal for temporal boundary classification: a paragraph from a later expansion-edit section than the subject's active-content expansion leans post_active_lore; earlier/same leans pre_entry/entry. Tokens match as substrings of the raw_section_role (e.g. 'mists' matches 'mists_of_pandaria_edit'). Order is meaningful here, unlike era_section_role_tokens which is a membership set. This deliberately encodes expansion chronology; it is a soft prior the LLM rubric can override, not a hard rule. Append the next expansion on release.
expansion_release_order._pilot_bias_note: All WoW expansions in release order, cross-zone. Announced-but-unreleased expansions (Midnight, The Last Titan) are included so forward-dated wiki edits are ranked.

historical_framing_markers._why_no_structural_signal: has_historical_framing scans free prose text for past-framing phrases; there is no section role or category attached to the text at that decision point.
historical_framing_markers._pilot_bias_note: Generic historical-framing phrases plus two WoW-era references ('third war'); broadly cross-zone. Statistical detection (tense) is handled separately by _PAST_TENSE_RE; this list catches explicit period phrasing.
